title: seva as vocation
hook: midday heat, cowherd boys resting in the shade, and Krishna starts praising the trees

segments.voice: Yesterday's word: seva as vocation. Not good deeds squeezed in around the job, but the job itself done as service. Whom did your work serve? Day one thousand two hundred nine.
screen: `THE JOB ITSELF AS SERVICE.` · `A TEACHER IN THE SHADE.`

segments.voice: Midday, far out in the forest, and the sun is fierce. Krishna and the cowherd boys have taken the cows a long way from the village, and the boys are hot and worn out. They duck under the trees for shade. Nobody here is studying anything. It's a rest stop, nothing more. And Krishna, instead of just resting, looks up into the branches and starts talking about the trees, the way you'd talk about a person you admire. It's in the Bhagavata's tenth book, a short scene in the middle of a summer day, and it holds a whole picture of service.
screen: `MIDDAY, FAR FROM THE VILLAGE.` → `BOYS IN THE SHADE.` → `KRISHNA PRAISES THE TREES.`

segments.voice: Look at these blessed trees, he says, in paraphrase. They live entirely for others. They put up with wind and rain, heat and frost themselves, and they shelter us from all of it. Then he lists what a tree gives: its leaves, flowers and fruit, its shade, its roots, bark and wood, its fragrance and sap, even its ashes, even its young shoots. No one who comes to a tree, he says, goes away with nothing. Then comes the verse that turns the scene into a teaching. This much, he says, is the fruit of being born: to keep doing good for others with your life, your wealth, your understanding and your words. Notice the four. Life, wealth, understanding, words. That's a list built for a vocation, because everyone has at least one of them. Some days the seva is money. Some days it's what you know. Some days it's showing up, life itself, your hours and your hands. And some days it's only a word, but a word is on the list. The tree doesn't pick one gift and refuse the rest. It gives whatever part of it is asked for. And notice who's listening. Not sages. Boys who look after cows. Krishna doesn't take them to a temple to learn about service. He points at the shade they're already sitting in.
screen: `THEY LIVE ENTIRELY FOR OTHERS.` · `LEAF, FRUIT, SHADE, BARK, EVEN ASH.` · `LIFE, WEALTH, UNDERSTANDING, WORDS.` · `A LESSON IN THE SHADE YOU SIT IN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: let the four gifts come one at a time. Settle, and breathe. Then go gently through Krishna's four. Life: where could your time help someone this week? Wealth: is there something small to give? Understanding: what do you know that someone needs? Words: who could use a kind one? Don't plan it all. Let one of the four light up, and rest there. If you pray, you can offer that one to the One you pray to. The bell holds the time.
Seva as vocation. Service as a life's work: like the tree, giving with life, wealth, understanding and words. Today's word.
Your line: seva as vocation. Today, give one of the four, your time, something you own, something you know, or a kind word, to someone who didn't ask. Day one thousand two hundred nine.

howItsDone: Hindu teachers point to Krishna's praise of the trees in the Bhagavata's tenth book as a picture of service, and its closing verse, on doing good with life, wealth, understanding and words, is recited in talks on seva.

fork.setup: you're one of the cowherd boys, hot and tired under a tree. Krishna starts talking. what does he point to?
options: the cows, and how to herd them better.
the trees, and how they live for others.
the village, and getting home before dark.
fork.reveal: he praises the trees: they bear the weather themselves, shelter others, and give every part of themselves away.

original.note: Sanskrit: tree; in this scene, Krishna's picture of a life lived for others.

trapdoor: what you thought: seva means giving money or volunteering time.
what it means: giving with whatever part of you is asked for, like a tree: life, wealth, understanding, words.
what a scholar hears: Bhagavata Purana 10.22.35, pranair arthair dhiya vaca: the fruit of a birth is always doing good with breath, wealth, intellect and speech.
recall: a warrior, and a daughter coming home
the year just walked and kept

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.22.30–31 (far from the village in the heat, the boys shelter under the trees)

Bhagavata Purana 10.22.35 (the fruit of birth: doing good with life, wealth, intellect and speech)

notes: Confirm verse numbers for 10.22.30–35 and the list of what the tree gives (the script follows the writer's recollection of 10.22.34).
10.22.35 transliterated in the trapdoor as 'pranair arthair dhiya vaca'; confirm.
'No one who comes to a tree goes away with nothing' paraphrases 10.22.33 (no supplicant leaves disappointed); confirm.
This scene sits just before the episode of the brahmins' wives (10.23); not mentioned in the script.
howItsDone: 'recited in talks on seva' is a general description; confirm or soften.

Editor pass: cut 'charcoal' from the tree's gifts (not clearly in 10.22.34; 'asthi' there is uncertain and left out); 'a lunch break' became 'a rest stop', since in 10.23 the boys have no food; the practice no longer opens 'sit like a tree for two minutes' (a number, and close to day 1203's 'sit like the ground').
